pr.title: Play field keys through a track's effects, routed into the daemon through FieldOut (live-supercollider.md chunk 3)
pr.head: f1d634d40428dcd81d4aafadd5294b7f627090b7

summary: field keys plays a SuperCollider instrument from the computer keyboard. Its sound comes from a voice host, sclang driving its own scsynth. A song's effects, the inserts on each track and on the tracks above it up to main, run in another process, the daemon field-audiod. So until now, playing a track's instrument with field keys sounded dry, and the instrument's line said so.

This pull request is chunk 3 of the live-supercollider plan, the chunk you hear. Chunk 1 (#196) taught a live session to read an input from outside the session and carry it up through every chain above its track. Chunk 2 (#198) added FieldOut, a SuperCollider plugin that writes audio into a shared-memory ring the daemon reads. This chunk connects the two. field keys <track> opens an input for each armed track, loads the song with those inputs, and has the voice host write each track's voice into its ring. With the transport stopped, the daemon now plays the inputs over silence.

Three rounds of review shaped this head. dc4d01c made an input close with the connection that opened it, kept the inputs through every other command's load, booted the voice host on the daemon's device, and put FieldOut on SC_PLUGIN_PATH. 269cb99 kept another terminal's loop, region, and solo, and ran glides on the overlay's own clock. f1d634d rewraps a docs paragraph and rebuilds the idle chain on stop and pause. It also refuses to route or reload under a take, and lets Ctrl-C quit while routing. The review of f1d634d confirmed all eleven earlier fixes and opened one P1. The idle chain's reset leaves its FIFO empty, so the next idle block crashes the daemon.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Voice host: sc/voice-host.scd running in sclang. It boots its own scsynth and turns MIDI into voices.
  • Input: a named source the daemon reads each block. field keys names its inputs keys:<song>/<track>.
  • Ring: the shared-memory buffer behind an input. FieldOut writes it and the daemon reads it.
  • FieldOut: the scsynth plugin that writes into a ring.
  • Route: the synth field-route, which carries one instrument's private bus into FieldOut.
  • Overlay: a second instance of each chain on an input's path, which the daemon runs beside the song.
  • Idle path: the overlay through a second instance of main's chain, played while the transport is stopped.
  • Converted delivery: the daemon resampling the song because the device cannot run at the song's rate.
  • Dry note: the end of the instrument's line, · dry: the effects on … are not heard.

cards.title: Review of f1d634d: changes requested
cards.html:
All eleven earlier threads are fixed and resolved. One is open:

  • Crash on stop or pause. resetIdle rebuilds the idle chain's limiter but leaves its FIFO empty. The next idle block reads past the FIFO and erases past its end, and field-audiod dies with SIGBUS. Reproduced with a limiter on main. The previous head survives the same steps.

cards.title: Left for later
cards.html:
• Criterion 3, hearing a track through its effects, is the author's to check by ear.
  • Criteria 4 and 5, the added latency and an hour without a dropout, need a real device.
  • A session swap under a playing input rebuilds the overlay cold, a gap of the path's latency. §10 accepts that for now.
  • The end-to-end test routing-voice.test.ts needs SuperCollider and an output device, so it skips on CI.

groups.title: What crosses between the processes
groups.kicker: The route SynthDef that Field writes, and the input's new peak in status
intro: Three processes take part when you play a track: field keys in Node, the voice host, and the daemon. This group holds the two small contracts between them that change.

The route is a SynthDef, SuperCollider's compiled synth definition. It reads two channels from a bus and hands them to FieldOut. sclang has no FieldOut class to build that SynthDef from, so routeSynthDef writes its binary form directly.
Each open input in the daemon's status now reports peak, the loudest sample read since a client last asked. Every client status read resets it.
A compiled session now names the track it soloed, if any, in an optional solo field, and the daemon reports it in status. That is how a command reloading the song can keep another terminal's solo.

files.note: The session gains an optional solo.
compileSession writes the solo it compiled with into the session.
Adds routeSynthDef: In.ar(in, 2) into FieldOut.ar(ring, …), with in and ring as controls.

groups.title: The daemon plays inputs while the song is stopped
groups.kicker: A second instance of the output chain, inputs that close with their connection, a peak meter, and a file-to-ring feeder
intro: Chunk 1 gave a live session input windows: a track reads audio from outside the session each block. What an input reaches travels in the overlay, a second instance of each chain on the input's path, summed into main, the output track, before main's own chain runs. Until now that happened only while the transport played.

With the transport stopped, Player::pullAudio now calls LiveSession::renderIdle when the session has inputs. It renders the overlay at the stopped position and runs it through idleChain, a second instance of the output track's chain. You hear what you play over silence, and the song's own chain and position stay where they were.

A gain ramp on a window the input passes through glides on overlayClock, a clock of the overlay's own that advances with every block the overlay renders. While the transport plays it keeps step with the song's clock. While it is stopped it still moves, so a fader moved then finishes its glide.

A stop or a pause rebuilds that second chain on the message thread, beside the output chain's own rebuild, so what you play next over silence carries nothing from before play. An input belongs to the connection that opened it: Server::dispatch passes the connection to Player::openInput as its owner, and the heartbeat's sweep of closed connections closes their inputs. Each input also meters its peak, and field-audiod --ring-feed <ring> <file.wav> writes a file into a ring at real-time pace, as FieldOut would.

An input now belongs to the connection that opened it. Server::dispatch passes the connection to Player::openInput as its owner, and the heartbeat's sweep of closed connections closes their inputs. A field keys that is killed therefore leaves nothing open, and the daemon still exits when idle. Each input also meters its peak, and field-audiod --ring-feed <ring> <file.wav> writes a file into a ring at real-time pace, as FieldOut would.

checks.text: A limiter or hosted plugin emits fewer samples than it takes while it fills its lookahead. Each chain's output therefore passes through a FIFO that starts with the chain's latency in zeros, so every block leaves whole and exactly that late (live-supercollider.md §9, step 4). idleDelayed is that FIFO for the idle chain.

files.note: Declares renderIdle, resetIdle, hasInputs, the idle chain's buffers, overlayClock, and each window's overlayRampStart.
Builds the idle chain at load, adds renderIdle and resetIdle, and evaluates the overlay's glides on overlayClock.

checks.text: resetIdle rebuilds the limiter, which then withholds its first capacity samples again. But std::fill only zeroes the FIFO's existing elements, and in steady state the FIFO is empty. The next renderIdle reads n samples from fewer, and erase(begin, begin + n) runs past the end. Reproduced at this head: with a limiter on main and a routed input, stop and pause each crashed the daemon with SIGBUS in renderIdle, leaving its rings in shared memory. The previous head survives the same steps.

Traced the glide: ramp sets overlayRampStart to overlayClock, each window is evaluated at overlayClock + i - overlayRampStart, and renderOverlay advances the clock by n after every block. Successive idle blocks therefore move the glide forward instead of restarting it.

Traced renderOverlay: it skips the chain for the output track, so overlay[slot].post is the sum before main's chain, and renderIdle applies that chain once. The FIFO starts with exactly the chain's latency, so a voice is as late with the transport stopped as playing.

Nothing here allocates on the audio thread. idleBlock and idleDelayed are reserved at load, 16384 frames plus the latency, and a block stays inside them. buildOverlay runs in the LiveSession constructor, and resetIdle runs on the message thread under the player's lock.

files.note: Declares closeInputsOwnedBy, keeps each open input with its owner in OpenInput, and holds the loaded session's solo.

Plays a stopped live session's inputs through renderIdle, resets the idle chain on stop and pause, records each input's owner, closes a connection's inputs, stamps each ring with the device's rate once a load has settled it, and reports the session's solo.

checks.text: The idle branch runs under the same ScopedTryLock on liveLock as the playing path, so it never reads a session in the middle of a swap.
Reproduced at this head: a process that routed and then exited without closing left no input open one second later, and the next routeArmed on that track routed.

files.note: dispatch takes the connection a request arrived on, as the owner of any input it opens.
Passes the connection to dispatch, and closes a connection's inputs when the sweep reaps it.

checks.text: The sweep runs on the daemon's 250 ms heartbeat, so a dropped connection's inputs close within about a quarter of a second.

files.note: Declares the peak, setSampleRate, and runRingFeed.
Tracks the loudest sample read, lets the player restamp the ring's rate, and adds runRingFeed for --ring-feed.

groups.title: The voice host writes into rings
groups.kicker: Each routed instrument's voices play into a private bus that its route carries into the ring
intro: The voice host is sc/voice-host.scd running in sclang. It boots its own scsynth and plays each armed instrument's voice from every MIDI source. Several instruments play in unison: each note sounds a voice from each.

VoiceHost.start now takes rings, one per instrument, each a ring number or null to play straight to the device. It also takes fieldOut, the directory that holds the built plugin. When any ring is set, it writes the route SynthDef to a temp file and passes FIELD_RINGS and FIELD_ROUTE_DEF to the host. It also puts FieldOut's directory on SC_PLUGIN_PATH, which scsynth searches beside its own plugins.

At each boot the host loads the route and gives each routed instrument a two-channel private bus. It then starts one route per bus at the tail of the default group, after every voice. A routed voice's out control is that bus, not bus 0.

scsynth crashes when it quits with a FieldOut still running, because it unloads plugins before it frees synths. So every way the host stops frees all nodes first. VoiceHost.close sends /g_freeAll before /quit, and both the rate restart and the parent-gone check call stopRoutes.

files.note: Starts and stops the routes, and sends each voice to its bus.

checks.text: A rate restart calls stopRoutes before server.quit. boot loads the route with d_load and runs startRoutes every time, so the routes come back on the new server with fresh buses.

files.note: Takes rings and fieldOut, writes the route SynthDef and removes it on close, puts FieldOut on SC_PLUGIN_PATH, finds the built FieldOut with fieldOutPluginDir, and frees all nodes before /quit.

checks.text: Non-realtime scsynth run with FieldOut only on SC_PLUGIN_PATH and no -U loaded the core UGens and FieldOut with no errors, and wrote into a daemon's ring. Checked on macOS at dc4d01c; this code is unchanged since. On Linux this rests on SuperCollider's source, where SC_PLUGIN_PATH is searched beside SC_PLUGIN_DIR.

Ran src/keys/voice-host.test.ts at this head. The host receives FIELD_RINGS, SC_PLUGIN_PATH, and a route file that starts with SCgf. That file is gone after close, and /g_freeAll reaches the server before /quit.

groups.title: field keys routes armed tracks through the daemon
groups.kicker: Open an input per track, load the song with them, and boot the voice host on the daemon's device
intro: field keys creek/track:bass arms the MIDI track bass and plays the instrument that the track names. Before this change, the voice always played straight to the device. The effects on bass and on the tracks above it were not heard, and the instrument's line ended with a dry note: · dry: the effects on keys-bus are not heard yet.
Now play calls routeArmed before the voice host starts, and it does four things:

1. Checks the device. It reads the daemon's device from status. If --device names another device, it plays dry with that reason.
  2. Opens an input for each armed track. It asks the daemon for an input named keys:<song>/<track>, which answers with a ring number.
  3. Loads the song with every open keys: input. It compiles the song with an input window for each input that keysInputsFor finds in status, its own and any other terminal's. It keeps the loaded session's loop, region, and solo, and loads the result. If the daemon then converts the song's rate, it closes its inputs and plays dry with that reason.
  4. Hands the rings and the device to the voice host. Each armed entry becomes its own instrument with its own ring, so two tracks that share an instrument still get separate voices. An instrument named without a track gets null and plays straight to the device.

When routing is not possible, routeArmed returns a reason, and the dry note always shows it. The note also names the effects on the way to the speakers, from main down to the MIDI track, which effectsAbove in targets.ts now adds. Once the voice is live, field keys checks that FieldOut is writing every ring. play runs the session in a try whose finally closes the inputs and loads the song again with whatever inputs others still hold.

files.note: New. routeArmed refuses under a take, checks the device, opens the inputs, loads the session with the loaded session's loop, region, and solo, checks for conversion, and returns the rings, the device, and a flowing check, or the reason it cannot. keysInputsFor lists the open keys: inputs for a song.

groups.title: Every command that loads the song keeps the inputs
groups.kicker: field play, its watch, field ui, and field record compile in the open keys: inputs
intro: An input window exists only in a compiled session. Without this group, any other command that loads the song, such as field play creek in another terminal, would compile it without the window, and the routed voice would go silent while its line still said the effects were heard.

Each of these commands now asks keysInputsFor for the song's open keys: inputs and compiles them in. field play does so before its first load. Its --watch asks again at each compile through a new inputs option of watchLiveSession. field ui asks at its first load and at every swap. field record asks when it loads the bed itself.

checks.text: Reproduced at this head: after routing, a load compiled with keysInputsFor, as these commands do, kept reading the ring, 23552 frames at peak 0.25 while stopped. routing.test.ts checks that the input stays listed after such a load.

files.note: Compiles the open keys: inputs into its first load, and passes keysInputsFor to its watch.
Takes an inputs callback and compiles what it returns at each recompile.
Compiles the open keys: inputs into its first load, every swap, and its watch.
Compiles the open keys: inputs into a bed it loads itself.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: From the instrument line up to a note through real sclang and scsynth
intro:
• routing.test.ts runs routeArmed against a null-output daemon, with an empty FieldOut.scx standing in for the build. It opens keys:creek/bass, loads creek with it, keeps it through another load, puts the song back on close, gives each reason it cannot route, and plays dry for a song the daemon converts.
  • routing-voice.test.ts runs the whole path through real sclang and scsynth with FieldOut: a note from a published MIDI source reaches the track's input. It needs SuperCollider and an output device, so it runs on a workstation and skips on CI.
  • live-ring.test.ts closes an input when its connection drops, feeds a ring with --ring-feed while the transport is stopped, reads the sine's 0.25 peak back through the idle path, and checks the route in a non-realtime scsynth.
  • voice-host.test.ts and keys.test.ts check what the host receives, the free before /quit, and the dry note.

checks.text: Ran eleven test files at this head with FIELD_AUDIOD set: routing, targets, live-ring, live-input, voice-host, keys, play-daemon, record-daemon, ui, ui-edits, and watch. All 113 tests passed, and every ring they opened was gone from shared memory afterward. No test stops or pauses with a routed input under a limiter, which is the case the open thread crashes on.
routing-voice.test.ts was read but not run in the review, because it opens the output device and connects every MIDI source.
